text:
Mikhail Sergachev is doing exactly what Utah traded for: 24:38 a night, 22 points in 24 games and 13 of them on the power play. Lately the minutes have climbed even higher, to 26:07 over his last ten, which tells you how much the Mammoth lean on him.

Some of the scoring will cool. He has six goals on 3.5 expected, shooting 10% after 6% last season, and our range for his finishing tops out at 8.7%. The setup work is the sturdier part: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.5 primary shot assists per 60 in 2025-26, 94th percentile among defensemen, and stopping 17% of the entries aimed at him against a typical 11%.

The worry is at five-on-five. Utah takes 54.6% of the expected goals with him out there, but 2.8 points less than when he sits, and the players he most resembles (Seth Jones, Noah Dobson, Filip Hronek) share the same note: chances against pile up. Evolving-Hockey rated him 0.7 wins above replacement last season, 88th among defensemen. The two-time Cup winner from Tampa projects to 71 points by our numbers, with a range of 59 to 83.
headline: Sergachev is running Utah's power play, and running hot
